cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, again. This message is for Aaron, Israel's high priest, and his sons, the priests: treat with respect the sacred offerings the Israelites have set apart for God. Friend, this isn't 'last cookie in the box' holy, this is HOLY holy.

cards.question: God tells Aaron and his sons to treat the sacred offerings with respect. Why?

answers.text: So they do not profane His holy name
So the people keep bringing more
So the altar stays clean and ready

cards.text: Then God gets specific. For generations to come, if any of Aaron's descendants comes near the sacred offerings while he's unclean, it's serious.

cards.question: What happens to a descendant of Aaron who approaches the sacred offerings while unclean?

answers.text: He must be cut off from God's presence
He must pay the priests in silver
He must leave the camp for a month

cards.text: If one of Aaron's descendants has a skin disease or a discharge, he may not eat the sacred offerings until he is clean.

Then God lists what a priest can touch that makes him unclean: anything defiled by a dead body, a crawling creature, whatever the uncleanness may be. Friend, after years in a junk drawer with the dust and the dead batteries, by these rules I'd have been unclean till next Tuesday.

cards.question: A priest who touches something defiled by a dead body or a crawling creature stays unclean until ___.
Before that priest can eat from the sacred offerings again, he has to bathe himself with water.

cards.text: Then the sun sets, and he's clean again, so he may eat from the sacred offerings. Sun goes down, uncleanness goes out, and that's the whole schedule.

cards.question: Once the priest is clean, God lets him eat from the sacred offerings. What reason does God give?

answers.text: Because they would go to waste
Because the people asked him to

cards.text: One more rule for the priests: they must not eat anything found dead or torn by wild animals. And God warns that the priests must keep His charge, or they'll bear the guilt and die.

cards.question: At the end of that warning, God says who makes the priests holy. Who is it?

cards.text: Now God sets the guest list for the sacred offering: no one outside a priest's family may eat it. Friend, that list is SHORT, almost as short as the list of who's allowed near my cookie dough, and that one's just me.

cards.question: A priest's guest or his hired hand may eat the sacred offering.
A slave ___ in the priest's household may eat the priest's food.

cards.text: What about a priest's daughter? If she marries a man who isn't a priest, she doesn't eat of the sacred contributions.

cards.question: If that daughter has no children, becomes widowed or divorced and comes back to her father's house, she may share her father's food again.

cards.text: And if someone eats a sacred offering by mistake, there's a way to make it right. I've grabbed the wrong cookie off the cooling rack before, friend, and all it cost me was a long talk with myself.

cards.question: Someone who eats a sacred offering in error must add a ___ to its value and give the sacred offering to the ___.
God tells the priests not to let the people eat the sacred offerings and so bear the punishment for guilt.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again. This time the message is for Aaron, his sons AND all the Israelites.
It's about anyone, even a foreign resident, who brings a burnt offering to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering. Burnt offering, friend, not burnt cookies, and I had to read that twice.

cards.question: What kind of animal must that burnt offering be for it to be accepted?

answers.text: The youngest animal in the herd

cards.text: And anything with a defect? God says it won't be accepted on their behalf.

cards.question: A peace offering for a vow or a freewill offering must also be without blemish or defect to be acceptable.

cards.text: Then God names what must not go on the altar: an animal that's blind, injured or maimed, or one with a running sore, a festering rash or a scab. I've had baking days, friend, where some of my cookies came out of the oven looking like that whole list.

cards.question: There's one exception. An ox or sheep with a deformed or stunted limb may be offered. As what kind of offering?
An ox or sheep with a deformed or stunted limb is acceptable to fulfill a vow.

cards.text: God names a few more injuries that rule an animal out, and none of them are to be sacrificed in the land. That goes for the Israelites, and it goes for a foreigner too.

cards.question: Why won't those injured animals be accepted on the people's behalf?

answers.text: Because they are deformed and flawed
Because they cost the giver too little
Because they belong to the priests

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again, and this time it's about animals that are just born.

cards.question: A newborn ox, sheep or goat must stay with its mother for ___ days.
From the eighth day on, that young animal is acceptable as a food offering to the LORD.

cards.text: One more rule about the animals: an ox or a sheep must not be slaughtered on the same day as its young.
Now the thank offering. God says to offer it so that it may be acceptable on their behalf.

cards.question: A thank offering can be saved and eaten over the next few days.

cards.text: Then God brings it all home: "You are to keep My commandments and practice them. I am the LORD." No fine print, friend. No 'terms may vary.'

cards.question: God says His holy name must not be profaned. What must happen among the Israelites instead?

answers.text: He must be acknowledged as holy
They must build Him a new altar
They must choose a new high priest

cards.question: At the very end, God reminds His people that He's the One who brought them out of the land of ___ to be their God.

cards.text: Keep that oven warm, friend. God still has more to say to His people about being holy.

findings.problem: The question depends on “that priest” in the previous card. It does not explain that this is a priest who became unclean by touching something defiling, so the statement is not self-contained.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: “At the end of that warning” points back to card 11 without telling the baker what the warning was. The question needs to supply the context of God warning the priests to keep His charge.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This card says that no one outside a priest's family may eat the sacred offering, directly settling card 14's question about the priest's guest and hired hand before that question is asked.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Leviticus 22:11 permits both a slave bought with the priest's own money and a slave born in his household to eat his food. The walkthrough teaches only the household-born slave, leaving the purchased-slave exception entirely covered nowhere.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: “That daughter” depends on card 16. The question never identifies her as a priest's daughter who married a man other than a priest, which is necessary context for the statement about sharing her father's food.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The answer reduces Leviticus 22:19 to “an unblemished male animal,” and no other card explains that it must be from the cattle, sheep, or goats. A baker could leave thinking any unblemished male animal qualifies.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The unrestricted statement that anything with a defect will not be accepted already rules out “False” on card 5, which asks whether a peace offering must also be without blemish or defect.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: “That young animal” and “the eighth day” depend on card 12. The question does not identify a newborn ox, sheep, or goat or explain that the eighth day is counted from its birth.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card runs beyond two sentences: the quotation itself contains two sentences, followed by the separate lines “No fine print, friend.” and “No 'terms may vary.'”

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
